subject: Phased SLO proposal and measurement windows for Datastream hosted API
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datastream.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@datastream.ai, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@datastream.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T08:15:00Z
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — what can Redwood commit to for p50/p95 and measurement windows?

Hi Soojin,

We're finalizing our Vendor SLO appendix for the Datastream enterprise contract and need concrete latency commitments and measurement definitions for your hosted inference API. Procurement has asked for the following details to include in the SOW:

- Numeric p50 and p95 targets (ms) per-request for standard text-generation workloads.
- How you measure those percentiles (sampling cadence, aggregation window, regional vs global).
- Any temporary relief or staged commitments during onboarding/cutover.
- Evidence package we can attach for the security/compliance review (metrics dashboard export, sampling logs).

A couple of constraints from our side: we have a hard go-live date of 2028-01-10 and anticipate an initial ramp to ~50k requests/day in month 1, 150k/day by month 3. We need the SLO language to be operationally verifiable by our SREs.

Can you send a proposed SLO clause and measurement definitions today? Also attached are our RFP questions (see datastream-rfp-questions.pdf) for context.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations
Datastream.ai

--- attachment: datastream-rfp-questions.pdf (application/pdf) ---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datastream.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-01T12:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — what can Redwood commit to for p50/p95 and measurement windows?

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. I discussed with Karthik and Lauren and put together a pragmatic proposal below that balances contractual clarity with the realities of initial ramp and model cutovers.

Proposal (high level) — phased commitments
1) Immediate (contract signature -> month 3):
   - p50: 80 ms per-request
   - p95: 500 ms per-request
   - Measurement: per-request latencies sampled continuously; p50 computed as the raw median of all sampled requests over a rolling 1-hour window, reported hourly. p95 computed as the 95th percentile over a sliding 30-minute window, with a daily rollup and a 7-day rolling percentile used for SLA evaluation.

2) Steady-state (month 4 onward, assuming normal traffic and no major infra/model cutovers):
   - p50: 60 ms per-request
   - p95: 450 ms per-request
   - Measurement: same sampling, but SLA evaluation will use a 7-day rolling percentile for both quantiles with a 24-hour aggregation checkpoint.

Temporary relief and carveouts
- Cutover carveout: For the first 72 hours after a major model change or region migration, we propose an automatic 24-hour carveout window where p95 is not counted towards SLA breaches (we will notify Datastream via the Console and via the agreed webhook).
- Monthly exceedance budget: during months 1–3 we allow up to 3 occurrence-days per month where p95 may exceed the Immediate threshold without breach, provided we supply a post-mortem and an operational remediation timeline.

Operational notes
- Region semantics: commitments above are regional (US East / US West). Failover requests routed to compatible model variants will be included in the measurement for the region they served.
- Evidence: we will provide a metric export (CSV) for each evaluation window plus a dashboard snapshot. See attached measurement-definitions.xlsx and the proposed SLO clause in redwood-hosted-slo-proposal-v2.pdf.

Next steps
- If the phased numbers look acceptable, we can insert the Immediate commitments into the SOW as an Appendix and add the Steady-state targets as a milestone (month 4).
- I’ve looped in Karthik for the technical detail piece and Lauren for commercial (billing/credits tied to breaches).

On that note — attaching the two files for your review. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the measurement windows.

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

--- attachments: redwood-hosted-slo-proposal-v2.pdf (application/pdf), measurement-definitions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) ---

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@datastream.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datastream.ai>, procurement@datastream.ai
Date: 2027-11-03T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — review comments

Thanks — this looks like a reasonable starting point. A few follow-ups from procurement and SRE: 

- Procurement wants the month-1 p95 number to be contractual (not just "Immediate") but is open to the monthly exceedance budget language if there's a clear credit/remediation mechanism. Can you propose a concrete credit table for breaches in months 1–3?
- SRE requests a short sample extract showing per-request data (timestamp, region, latency_ms, model_id) for a 24-hour window so we can validate the measurement script. Is that something you can provide as anonymized sample data?
- Also confirm how the carveout is triggered and whether Datastream can request an investigation within that 24-hour window.

If we can get those items by EOD Friday (2027-11-05) procurement will circulate a draft SOW with your proposed Appendix.

– Marta
VP Operations, Datastream.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-04T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — phased SLO + next steps

Alex / Marta — quick update and next steps:

1) Credit table: see below for a starter (we can map to $ credits or % invoice credits in the SOW):
   - Month 1–3: single daily breach of p95 Immediate -> 2% invoice credit for that month; 2+ breach-days in a month -> 6% credit and an escalation runbook.
   - Month 4+: each monthly window breach -> 5% credit; repeated >2 months triggers a remediation SLA and potential termination rights per the SOW.

2) Anonymized sample: Karthik will create a 24-hour anonymized extract with the fields you requested and deliver by EOD 2027-11-05.

3) Carveout trigger and investigation: carveout is automatic for platform-triggered major model change/region migration (we will post a Console notice and send webhook). Datastream can request an investigation within the 24-hour carveout window; if requested, we will pause the automatic carveout and treat the window as "under investigation" while we gather evidence (we will still provide the sample extract).

If this aligns, I’ll ask Legal to prepare the Appendix language and Lauren to add the credit table into the commercial term sheet. Happy to take a 30-minute call Friday at 10:00 PT to finalize.

Thanks,
Soojin
